title: Payments and Invoice Credits on Resort Club Memberships Accounts
content:
Invoices on a Resort Club Memberships account are paid by automatic card payment where the level requires it, each payment naming the invoice it pays.

## Credits

A credit is given only for an invoice that should not have been raised:

1. dues invoiced for a month in which the membership was frozen;
2. dues or charges invoiced for a period after the termination date;
3. a second dues invoice for the same billing period.

The credit is the full amount of that invoice, or the part of a prorated month outside the membership. Each invoice is credited at most once. Goodwill credits, credits for facilities a member chose not to use, and refunds of initiation fees are outside these rules.

## How payments and credits appear

| Entry | What it names | Effect on the dues balance |
|---|---|---|
| Payment | The invoice it pays | Reduces the amount owed |
| Credit | The invoice it credits | Reduces the amount owed |

The dues balance is the amount the member owes the club: fees, dues and member charges invoiced, less payments and credits.

## Credit decision table

| Invoice under review | Credit under these rules | Amount of the credit |
|---|---|---|
| Dues invoice for a month the membership was frozen | Yes | Full amount of the invoice |
| Dues or a charge invoiced for a period after the termination date | Yes | Full amount of the invoice |
| Second dues invoice for a billing period already invoiced | Yes | Full amount of the second invoice |
| Invoice for a prorated month partly outside the membership | Yes, for the part outside | The part of the prorated month outside the membership |
| Invoice already credited once | No | — |
| Request for a goodwill credit | Outside these rules | — |
| Request for a credit for a facility the member chose not to use | Outside these rules | — |
| Refund of an initiation fee | Outside these rules | — |

## Example (hypothetical)

A member's account shows two dues invoices for the same month, each of 189.00. The second invoice should not have been raised: it is credited in full, 189.00, by one credit naming it. The first invoice stands, and once the second invoice has been credited it cannot be credited again.
